name: Omri
charge: Doing worse than all that were before him; walking in all the way of Jeroboam
summary: After Zimri’s seven days Israel was split between Tibni and Omri, the captain of the host; Omri’s side prevailed, and he reigned twelve years (1 Kings 16:21-23). He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver and built the city that became the capital of the northern kingdom, yet he did worse than all before him, walking in all the way of Jeroboam (1 Kings 16:24-26). His son Ahab brought in Baal, and the prophets later named the whole corruption after them both: the statutes of Omri and the works of the house of Ahab (Micah 6:16).
offenseFull: When Zimri burnt the palace over himself, the people of Israel were divided in two: half followed Tibni the son of Ginath to make him king, and half followed Omri. Those who followed Omri prevailed, Tibni died, and Omri reigned (1 Kings 16:21-22). In the thirty-first year of Asa he began to reign over Israel, twelve years, six of them in Tirzah (1 Kings 16:23). He bought the hill Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, built a city on it, and named it after Shemer, the owner of the hill (1 Kings 16:24). The Samaritan Woman teaching begins its whole account here: from that time Samaria was the capital city of the northern kingdom, the head of Ephraim (Isaiah 7:9), and the land of the ten tribes that revolted from the house of David. When Christ met the woman at the well in Sychar, a city of Samaria near the ground Jacob gave to Joseph, he was speaking to a daughter of that kingdom (John 4:4-9).

But Omri did evil in the eyes of the Lord, worse than all who were before him, for he walked in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat and in the sin he made Israel commit, provoking the Lord God of Israel with their vanities (1 Kings 16:25-26). The teachers observe that there were no righteous kings in the northern kingdom from Jeroboam all the way down; every time a king of Israel is named, the record says he did evil in the sight of the Lord. History in the AM counts Omri as the sixth king of the north, after Jeroboam, Nadab, Baasha, Elah and Zimri.
judgmentFull: Omri died and was buried in Samaria, the city he had bought, and Ahab his son reigned in his place (1 Kings 16:27-28). History in the AM says Omri built Samaria into a rich city, a northern Jerusalem, through an alliance with the Zidonians of Tyre and Zidon, and sealed it by marrying his son to their daughter. Ahab did evil above all before him, and as if the sins of Jeroboam were a light thing, he married Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians and served Baal, raising an altar to Baal in the house of Baal he built in Samaria (1 Kings 16:30-32). So idol worship was established in the very city Omri built.

Generations later Micah gave the verdict by name. The rich were violent and the people liars, so the Lord would strike them and leave them desolate; they would sow and not reap and press olives without oil, because they still kept the statutes of Omri and all the works of the house of Ahab and followed their counsel, and so they would carry the reproach of His people (Micah 6:12-16). Injurious Practices in the Kingdom asks why Micah names Omri and Ahab, and answers that the works of idolatry, marriage to the heathen and every other wickedness set up in their days were still being kept in the land. Amos warned that those who swear by the sin of Samaria and say the god of Dan lives would fall and never rise again (Amos 8:14). The land of Samaria that Omri bought was the land the northern kingdom was carried away out of, when the king of Assyria besieged it three years and took it in the ninth year of Hoshea (2 Kings 17:5-6).

For he walked in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin, to provoke the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.

And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established.
And he must needs go through Samaria.
Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
Now Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus on the well: and it was about the sixth hour.
There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink.
(For his disciples were gone away unto the city to buy meat.)
Then saith the woman of Samaria unto him, How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.
But Omri wrought evil in the eyes of the Lord, and did worse than all that were before him.
For he walked in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin, to provoke the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
Now the rest of the acts of Omri which he did, and his might that he shewed, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
So Omri slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria: and Ahab his son reigned in his stead.
And Ahab the son of Omri did evil in the sight of the Lord above all that were before him.

And it came to pass, as if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, that he took to wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshipped him.
And he reared up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal, which he had built in Samaria.
For the rich men thereof are full of violence, and the inhabitants thereof have spoken lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.
Therefore also will I make thee sick in smiting thee, in making thee desolate because of thy sins.
Thou shalt eat, but not be satisfied; and thy casting down shall be in the midst of thee; and thou shalt take hold, but shalt not deliver; and that which thou deliverest will I give up to the sword.
Thou shalt sow, but thou shalt not reap; thou shalt tread the olives, but thou shalt not anoint thee with oil; and sweet wine, but shalt not drink wine.

For the statutes of Omri are kept, and all the works of the house of Ahab, and ye walk in their counsels; that I should make thee a desolation, and the inhabitants thereof an hissing: therefore ye shall bear the reproach of my people.
They that swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, Thy god, O Dan, liveth; and, The manner of Beer–sheba liveth; even they shall fall, and never rise up again.
Then the king of Assyria came up throughout all the land, and went up to Samaria, and besieged it three years.
In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
